title: Home practical guide and safety card: salt crystals
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
unit: Spring 2: Transport, the periodic table and waves
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 92 (Home practical guide and safety card: salt crystals (portal worksheet; warm tap water only, adult present))
intro: Lesson 92: Preparing copper(II) sulfate crystals. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To grow salt crystals (modelling the copper sulfate method)
safety: Warm tap water only, adult present
An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Stir salt into warm tap water until no more dissolves (saturated)
Pour the clear solution into a clean jar, leaving undissolved salt behind
Tie string to a pencil and hang it in the jar
Leave somewhere warm and still for several days
Do not taste; an adult is present
Draw the crystals and explain why they form

questions.q: Big question: how do black and colourless make blue?
questions.a: A new substance forms; copper(II) ions in the salt give the blue colour.
